newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium seen probing upside.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper, aluminium seen probing upside.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper bounced above $2,400 a tonne in late trading on Wednesday, but still needs to hurdle resistance at $2,440-$2,450 to strengthen the charts, analysts and dealers said on Thursday.
Aluminium was trending up, with the recent high of $1,628 pegged as the near-term target, they added.
COPPER - Prices were firmer after a speculative rally late on Wednesday and more gains were likely on Thursday, traders said.
The cash/threes backwardation, which flared out to $150/$159 on Thursday morning, was also helping boost prices.
"There's still some possible tightness in July dates -- I'm not bearish here," a trader noted.

However, prices would meet interim resistance at around $2,420, which needed to be overcome before copper could tackle $2,440 -- the previous high and the position of the 10-day moving average, analysts said.
At 0800 GMT three months copper was quoted at $2,408/12, up $18 from Wednesday's kerb close.
ALUMINIUM - With technical indicators pointing higher, aluminium was gearing up to take a crack at the previous high of $1,628, analysts said.

"However, there are signs of indecision and the market really needs to breach $1,620 and then $1,635 for further upwards momentum," brokers Brandeis said in a commentary, which also pegged nearby support at $1,602.
At 0800 GMT three months aluminium was at $1,617/20, up $7 from Wednesday's kerb close.
